assessment: Phosphorylated Tau (pTau) aggregation into neurofibrillary tangles is closely associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), and this process is mediated by several molecular chaperones. The authors dissect the important molecular mechanism of the interplay between Hsp27 and pTau, which is relevant to pathology, using a combination of approaches including a Drosophila tauopathy model, and biophysical and computational methods. This work provides fundamental molecular insights into the important role of Hsp27 in preventing pTau pathology in AD.
